requirement.original: Is the kill step in restore_online_sessions() necessary? Can the same session (same Claude UUID) be spawned twice simultaneously?
requirement.clarified: Investigate whether duplicate session spawning is possible across all layers (recovery script, daemon, Claude SDK, server) and whether the kill step is a necessary safeguard.
requirement.what: Investigation into duplicate session spawn possibility
requirement.why: Determine if kill step in restore_online_sessions() can be safely removed or must be kept
success_criteria: Clear YES/NO answer on whether duplicates are possible
Evidence from each layer with file paths and line numbers
Recommendation on whether kill step should be kept
constraints: Must not break existing recovery flow

root_cause_analysis.symptom: Question about whether kill step in restore is necessary
root_cause_analysis.root_cause: No deduplication mechanism exists at any layer - daemon tracks by PID not UUID, Claude SDK has no file locking, server creates separate sessions per random tag
root_cause_analysis.why_introduced: Daemon was designed to track sessions by PID for simplicity; UUID dedup was never implemented
root_cause_analysis.why_problematic: Without the kill step, orphan processes + new spawns would create duplicate sessions visible to users

investigation_results.answer: YES - duplicates ARE possible. The kill step IS necessary.

daemon_spawn_session_endpoint.evidence: No UUID check before spawning; passes directly to spawnSession()

daemon_spawnSession_function.evidence: pidToTrackedSession is keyed by PID, not UUID. No check for existing sessions with same Claude UUID.

recovery_script_daemon_spawn_session.evidence: Spawns via systemd-run/nohup directly, no daemon /list check before spawn

claude_sdk_resume.evidence: --resume is a CLI flag, no file locking on .jsonl. Claude forks session: creates new UUID, new .jsonl file with copied history.

server_session_creation.evidence: Tag idempotency uses @@unique([accountId, tag]), but each process uses randomUUID() as tag (runClaude.ts:82), so no collision

websocket_connections.evidence: Each process creates independent sessionSyncClient with own WebSocket. Server handles both.

duplicate_scenario.description: Orphan alive + restore spawns same UUID
duplicate_scenario.old_process: Continues running with existing Claude process, connected to happy-server session X
duplicate_scenario.new_process: Claude forks UUID-A into UUID-B, creates happy-server session Y with randomUUID() tag
duplicate_scenario.result: Two sessions visible in app, duplicate conversation history, user confusion

kill_step_justification: Prevents duplicate sessions (no dedup at any layer)
Ensures new daemon tracks all sessions (old processes not registered with new daemon's pidToTrackedSession)
Old processes cannot report via webhook (daemon HTTP port changed after restart)

research_findings.reason: Pure codebase investigation - no external best practices needed

development_approach.strategy: Investigation only - no code changes needed
development_approach.validation_approach: Code reading and logical analysis across all layers

optional_improvements.description: Add UUID-based dedup to spawnSession() in run.ts
optional_improvements.rationale: Defense-in-depth: check pidToTrackedSession for matching claudeSessionId before spawning

optional_improvements.description: Add /list check in daemon_spawn_session() before spawning
optional_improvements.rationale: Belt-and-suspenders: query daemon for running sessions before spawning
